For real-time camera gesture recognition using fastdtw and MediaPipe: 1) Never run fastdtw in the main camera thread as it drops FPS drastically; use a background thread. 2) Using fastdtw's built-in dist=2 is ~10x faster than using a python distance callback like scipy.spatial.distance.euclidean. 3) Implement a 'missed_frames' grace period (e.g., 15 frames, or 0.5s) before clearing the gesture frame buffer when MediaPipe momentarily loses tracking, to prevent a brittle user experience.

SIH_ISL_2026 performance deep-test findings (August 2026): The primary bottleneck in the buffer/frame rendering system is NOT GPU acceleration (correctly configured with delegate:'GPU', COOP/COEP headers present). The real culprits are: (1) Math.sqrt() called inside the innermost DTW loop in dtwWorker.ts L140 — mathematically unnecessary for ranking and costs ~15-30% of DTW time; (2) getRingBufferSnapshot() creates a full copy on every match attempt despite dtwDistance() already supporting start/length params; (3) The rAF detection loop useEffect depends on drawLandmarks which changes identity when showMesh/demoState changes, causing loop restarts and visible stutter. Feature vector parity between Python and TS is confirmed correct (106-dim, same normalization). The 1.0-x mirroring in TS is intentional for CSS scaleX(-1) compensation.
